title: ר' ברכיה בר' סימון

paragraphs: Rabbi Berekhiah, son of Rabbi Simon, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, swallowed a creeping creature. A sectarian whispered an incantation over him and it came out. He said, “Would that he should die and not hear this”; and it happened “as in an inadvertent error …” [the witness reads כשגנה], and he died in holiness. The Arukh, entry balam, writes this in the name of the midrash at the end of Eikhah. It is not there, but rather in Kohelet Rabbah, on the verse “There is an evil I have seen.” There the reading is “the son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,” whereas the Arukh’s reading is “the son of the son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.” This is the wording of Midrash Kohelet: he had something swallowed; he went and brought one of those of the house of …, to remove what he had swallowed by an incantation. Afterwards Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi asked that man, “What did you say over him?” He told him a certain verse [the source reads וא״כ]. He said, “It would have been preferable for him to bury his son rather than for you to say this verse.” So it happened: his son died, “like an inadvertent error …” There too, Rav Yirmeyah of Deshavshav (see his entry) took a wreath of olive branches and tied it on his head. Shmuel heard and said, “It would have been better for his head to be taken off than for him to do this.” So it happened to him. All this is in Midrash Kohelet. The aforementioned story of Rabbi Yirmeyah of Deshavshav is also in Midrash Eikhah, on the verse “The crown has fallen from our head.” This caused the author of the Arukh’s mistake: he thought that the story of the grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi too was written adjacent to it in Midrash Eikhah. Understand this.
